text.p: The following are the main stories from Friday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG

- Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel says he expects his Free Democrats (FDP) to go into election campaign alongside current coalition partners, Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats, but without a formal coalition agreement.
- Situation in flood-threatened eastern Germany getting more serious by the day.
- Former East German leader Egon Krenz says Moscow was to blame for shootings at Berlin Wall.
- Industry calls on government to push forward expansion of German airports.
HANDELSBLATT
- Bonn paying 80 percent of net contributions to European Union budget, data from EU commission shows.
- Giant Kirch group wants to pursue more open policy towards media.
- German Trade Union Federation (DGB) leader Dieter Schulte pledges higher wage demands if labour market situation does not improve this year.
- Half-year results for Commerzbank and Bayerischer Vereinsbank point to further rise in profits in 1997.
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- Number of divorces in Germany reaches record high.
- Around 8,300 soldiers now in flood-hit area to help with rescue operation.
- Constitutiional court rejects appeal by East German generals against convictions for killings at the border between two Germanys.
- Bonn warns hospitals they will have to settle for less income in future.
- Higher prescription charges and new tax rates for car owners push west German inflation higher in July.
DIE WELT
- Opposition Social Democrats warn against big hike in value-added tax.
- Bonn imposes new limits on employing workers from central and eastern Europe.
- Lower rents and high number of new homes means more people are moving house in Berlin.
